rules.rule: No gradients or large saturated fills
rules.why: Color on a large area pulls the eye away from the content.
rules.avoid: Gradients; large saturated fills
rules.do: A neutral surface; color on one small thing

rules.rule: Nothing is bigger than the page title
rules.why: Size is the last tool for hierarchy. A banner or a number larger than the title takes over the page.
rules.avoid: Text larger than the page title (big metrics, banners)
rules.do: `text-heading` at most; `text-metric` for a tile number; `text-display` only on Home, first-run hero screens, and auth and error pages

rules.rule: No all caps, exclamation marks or emoji
rules.why: The product speaks plainly. Sentence case reads faster than capitals.
rules.avoid: ALL CAPS, exclamation marks, emoji
rules.do: Sentence case, plain words

rules.rule: Icons take the text color
rules.why: A colored icon competes with the text next to it.
rules.avoid: Colored icons outside status
rules.do: The text color; only a status icon takes its status color

rules.rule: One highlight color per screen
rules.why: One highlight tells the user where to look. Several cancel each other out.
rules.avoid: Several highlight colors on one screen
rules.do: One highlight: the brand action or one status

rules.rule: Thin lines, soft shadows
rules.why: A heavy frame is louder than its content.
rules.avoid: Lines of 2px or more; hard or colored shadows
rules.do: 1px lines; 2px only for focus, the active tab underline and a diff or recent-change gutter marker; translucent shadows on floating things only

rules.rule: Use a theme variable, never a raw color
rules.why: A variable names a job, so the same job gets the same color everywhere. A raw value drifts with the next person.
rules.avoid: Raw hex, stock Tailwind colors, antd names (`colorBg*`, `--ag-color*`); a text color used as a border (`border-muted-foreground`)
rules.do: A theme variable: `bg-muted`, `text-muted-foreground`; a border takes `border`, `border-muted` or `border-strong`

rules.rule: Brand yellow marks the one brand action
rules.why: The yellow is the strongest color. On several things it points at nothing, and in dark `primary` is yellow too.
rules.avoid: Brand yellow on badges, highlights, Publish, sign-in, billing, or more than one button
rules.do: `brand` only on New agent on Home; the default primary elsewhere

rules.rule: Status needs a word or an icon
rules.why: About 1 in 12 men see red and green poorly. Color only supports the meaning.
rules.avoid: Status shown by a colored dot alone
rules.do: A tint and a word, with an icon where it fits

rules.rule: No dark-mode colors in a component
rules.why: A theme variable already changes per theme. A component's own dark color drifts from the theme.
rules.avoid: A component that sets its own dark-mode color (`.dark .menu {…}`)
rules.do: A theme variable whose value changes per theme (`popover`)

rules.rule: UI colors stay neutral; data colors are for data
rules.why: A color for one component adds a palette nobody controls. A data color on UI state reads as a category.
rules.avoid: A new color for one component; a data color for selected, hover, status or a button; a color per workspace or project Mark
rules.do: One of the 23 UI colors or a tint of one; `data-1` … `data-6` only for categories and chart series, in order; the current workspace Mark takes `bg-brand/15`, and an agent Mark may take a data color

rules.rule: Use the text styles, never a pixel size
rules.why: Each near-miss size looks a little wrong next to the real ones. One screen had 35 sizes.
rules.avoid: Arbitrary sizes: `text-[13px]`, `text-[15px]`, 13.5px
rules.do: One of the text styles

rules.rule: Show importance with weight and tone, not size
rules.why: A bigger size breaks the scale and makes the line taller.
rules.avoid: A bigger size to show importance
rules.do: Weight 500 and `foreground`; quiet the rest with `muted-foreground`

rules.rule: Numbers in columns use tabular figures
rules.why: Proportional digits move a column of numbers left and right.
rules.avoid: Proportional digits in columns
rules.do: `tabular-nums`

rules.rule: No weight above 600
rules.why: Bold text shouts.
rules.avoid: `font-bold`, weight 700 or more, `<strong>` in the interface
rules.do: 600 for titles only, 500 for emphasis

rules.rule: Weight never changes with state
rules.why: A bolder word is wider, so the label and its neighbors move. Weight already means rank.
rules.avoid: A control that turns bolder when active, selected, current, open or focused (`data-[state=active]:font-semibold`); a 600 button
rules.do: Weight 500 (`text-label`) in every state; state shows by color or a fill (`bg-selected`, `text-foreground`)

rules.rule: Pass a size, never a height
rules.why: A control owns its height, padding, radius, text and icon. A height class breaks that on one screen.
rules.avoid: Height classes on controls: `h-[34px]`, `h-[30px]`
rules.do: The `size` prop

rules.rule: Nothing gets bigger on a compact window or on touch
rules.why: Bigger controls make every screen bulky: the toolbar no longer fits and lists show half the rows. The kit already steps down below 640px.
rules.avoid: `phone ? "h-11"`, `pointer-coarse:size-11`, `max-md:h-11`, `[&_button]:min-h-11`, 44px rows, hidden tap boxes
rules.do: The same kit sizes everywhere; they step down below 640px by themselves

rules.rule: Only things round by nature are round
rules.why: One shape family makes every component look like one product. A pill button or a circle Mark next to a 6px control reads as a second system. A status dot, a switch and a radio are round by nature, and a square one looks wrong.
rules.avoid: A round button, input, badge, chip, tag, Mark, card or menu; a pill; `rounded-full` or `50%` anywhere; a square status dot, switch, radio or slider handle
rules.do: Controls and containers: `radius-sm` or `radius-md`, at most a quarter of the short side. Status dots, typing dots, the switch, the radio and the slider handle: `rounded-round`. Icons are drawings and keep their own curves

rules.rule: Nested corners are concentric
rules.why: With the same radius inside and out, the gap is wider at the corners than on the sides.
rules.avoid: The same radius inside and outside a padded box
rules.do: Inner radius = outer radius − padding

rules.rule: Phosphor, regular weight, only
rules.why: Phosphor's thin round strokes next to heavier ones look like two products.
rules.avoid: `lucide-react` or a second icon library; a filled icon that does not show a state
rules.do: Phosphor, regular weight; `fill` only to show a state

rules.rule: One icon per button
rules.why: A second icon makes the button look like two controls.
rules.avoid: Two icons in one button
rules.do: One icon: leading, or a trailing caret on a menu trigger

rules.rule: Center icons by eye
rules.why: A play triangle or an arrow looks off-center when its box is centered.
rules.avoid: Play and arrow icons centered by their box
rules.do: Move them 1px so they look centered

rules.rule: Icon size comes from the place
rules.why: An icon picked per screen looks wrong next to the text beside it.
rules.avoid: 18 or 20px icons next to 13px text
rules.do: 12, 14 or 16px, by the `usage` of the `icon-*` sizes in `theme.config.ts`

rules.rule: One icon per product term
rules.why: When a term has two icons, users read two different things.
rules.avoid: Skill as a compass in the nav and a book in a list
rules.do: The icon from the terms list in `rules.json`; bare in nav and menus, inside a Mark in lists, pickers and headers; any Phosphor regular icon for a generic action (Plus, Trash, Copy)

rules.rule: Separate areas by tone
rules.why: Each border is one more line to read.
rules.avoid: Borders around borders to separate areas
rules.do: A different surface tone

rules.rule: Draw each border once
rules.why: Two bordered boxes stacked draw a 2px seam.
rules.avoid: Two bordered boxes stacked
rules.do: One border, with a divider inside

rules.rule: Shadows only on things that float
rules.why: A shadow says this sits above the page.
rules.avoid: Shadows on flat cards and list items; opaque gray shadows
rules.do: `shadow-overlay`, `shadow-modal`, `shadow-raised`, on floating things only

rules.rule: Hover never lifts
rules.why: A shadow on hover says the element moved up, not that it is hovered.
rules.avoid: A shadow or a lift on hover
rules.do: The hover fill

rules.rule: One hover fill
rules.why: `accent` is ink at 5%, so it is the same step darker on the page, in the sidebar and in a popover.
rules.avoid: `hover:bg-muted`, `hover:bg-foreground/10`, a gray picked per screen
rules.do: `hover:bg-accent`; on a sticky row that must stay opaque, `accent` over the ground as a gradient image

rules.rule: Nothing inside a row has the hover fill
rules.why: A fill that matches the hover disappears when the row is hovered.
rules.avoid: A fill inside a row that matches the hover fill
rules.do: A translucent fill (`secondary`) that stacks on the hover

rules.rule: Space from the 4px scale, tighter inside groups
rules.why: Less space inside a group than between groups shows the groups without lines.
rules.avoid: Off-scale gaps (11px); even spacing that hides groups
rules.do: `gap-1/2/3/4/6/8`; less space inside a group than between groups

rules.rule: Grouped buttons sit 4px apart, 8px at most
rules.why: A group reads as one unit only when its gap is smaller than the space around it.
rules.avoid: Grouped buttons 12px or more apart
rules.do: `gap-1`; `gap-2` at most

rules.rule: Icon to text: 4, 6 or 8px by place
rules.why: The gap follows the place, so the same element looks the same everywhere.
rules.avoid: Icon-to-text gaps picked per screen (1, 10, 12px)
rules.do: 4px in badges and `xs` buttons, 6px in other controls, 8px in rows

rules.rule: Mark to text: 8 or 12px
rules.why: A bigger Mark needs more room, and the same Mark always gets the same gap.
rules.avoid: Mark-to-text gaps picked per screen
rules.do: 8px for 16–24px Marks, 12px for 32–40px Marks

rules.rule: Equal visible gaps between icons
rules.why: Icons differ in width, so gaps measured from their boxes look uneven.
rules.avoid: Icons in a row spaced by their boxes
rules.do: Equal gaps between the visible icon edges

rules.rule: One row height per list
rules.why: Rows of one height make a list easy to scan.
rules.avoid: List rows other than 28, 36 and 48px; mixed heights in one list; a divider below the row's height
rules.do: `row-dense` for tree and rail rows, `row-single`, `row-double`; the divider inside the height

rules.rule: Every menu row is `MENU_ITEM`
rules.why: A menu, a select and a combobox are the same thing to a user.
rules.avoid: Menu rows with their own height, padding or text (a 28px dropdown, a 36px option)
rules.do: `MENU_ITEM`: 32px, 8px side padding, `text-label`, a 16px icon

rules.rule: A search popover has one shape
rules.why: Users learn the layout once.
rules.avoid: A search popover with a tall search, rows on other edges, or a big button as the action
rules.do: Search on top, group headings, `MENU_ITEM` rows, a divider, then the action as one more row

rules.rule: Rows in a list are 2, 4 or 8px apart, by row height
rules.why: A small gap lets each row's hover fill stand on its own, and the gap grows with the row, so tall rows with a Mark and two lines do not crowd each other.
rules.avoid: Two-line rows that touch; a gap picked per screen (6px, 12px); more than 8px between rows of one list
rules.do: `gap-0.5` (2px) between dense rows: menus, the sidebar, trees and rails · `gap-1` (4px) between one-line rows (`row-single`) · `gap-2` (8px) between two-line rows (`row-double`): the Home lists and the Agents, Skills and Automations tables · no gap in a table whose rows are split by divider lines

rules.rule: One primary action per view
rules.why: The primary button answers "what do I do here?". Two give two answers.
rules.avoid: Two primary buttons in one view
rules.do: One primary; the rest `secondary`, `outline` or `ghost`

rules.rule: Label a button with its action
rules.why: A verb and an object say what happens. OK makes the user read the dialog again.
rules.avoid: "OK", "Submit", "Yes"
rules.do: Verb + object: "Delete agent"

rules.rule: Destructive actions stay quiet until the confirm
rules.why: A solid red button on a page is louder than the primary action.
rules.avoid: A solid red button on a page, in a toolbar or in a menu
rules.do: `destructive-ghost`; solid `destructive` only to confirm in a dialog; in a menu, destructive items come last, after a separator

rules.rule: Field help goes in a "?" tooltip
rules.why: Help under every label doubles the height of the form.
rules.avoid: Help text under every label
rules.do: `Field` with `tooltip`: the "?" opens on hover, on focus and on a tap

rules.rule: One focus style
rules.why: Focus that looks different per control is easy to lose.
rules.avoid: A gray halo, `outline-4`, `ring-[3px]`, an offset gap
rules.do: `focus-ring` on any control (a 2px `ring` outline with a 1px `foreground` line inside), `focus-ring-field` on a bordered field, `focus-ring-inset` on a full-bleed row inside a scroller; all three are in `@agenta/ui/focus.css`

rules.rule: Focus the field the user came to fill
rules.why: A click to reach the only field is a wasted step. When typing is the next step, the keyboard that opens on touch is wanted.
rules.avoid: The user must click into the field; autofocus on a page the user only reads
rules.do: Autofocus it when typing is the next step: a New dialog, a rename, a search the user opened

rules.rule: An empty state says what to do next
rules.why: "Nothing here" is a dead end.
rules.avoid: "No data", "Nothing here"
rules.do: What is missing, why it matters, one first action (`EmptyState`)

rules.rule: The skeleton matches the loaded view
rules.why: Another layout makes the page jump when the data arrives.
rules.avoid: A spinner or generic bars for a list
rules.do: A skeleton with the loaded layout (`Skeleton`, `SkeletonBlock`, `SkeletonRows`)

rules.rule: An error says what happened and the fix
rules.why: "Something went wrong" gives the user nothing to act on.
rules.avoid: "Something went wrong"
rules.do: Cause, effect, fix, in an `Alert` next to the problem

rules.rule: One alignment line; only a hover fill hangs outside it
rules.why: The eye follows what it sees at rest: text, the edge of a field, a Mark. The hover fill of a row is not visible at rest, so when its box starts on the line, the Mark inside drifts right by the padding of the row.
rules.avoid: A field pushed out left of the line; the box of a row on the line, so its Mark and the column label drift right
rules.do: The title, the description, the edge of a field, the labels and the first Mark of each row on the line; a row or a nav item hangs its hover fill outside by its own padding (row 12, nav item 8); the screen sets the negative margin, since the kit does not yet

rules.rule: Sidebar rows share two lines: the icon line and the text line
rules.why: The eye reads the rail down its edges. Icons, the Mark and icon-less rows on one edge, and the labels of icon rows on a second, keep the rail one column instead of a staircase.
rules.avoid: Sidebar icons off the workspace Mark's edge; group labels or session rows indented to their own line; nav text and the workspace name on different lines
rules.do: The 16px workspace Mark and every 16px icon on the icon line (16px from the rail edge); their labels on the text line (40px); rows and labels with no icon (group labels, sessions) start on the icon line

rules.rule: One scroll container per pane
rules.why: Two areas that scroll the same way trap the scroll wheel.
rules.avoid: Nested scroll areas that scroll the same way
rules.do: One scroll container per pane

rules.rule: Cap the content width
rules.why: Text across a wide window is hard to read.
rules.avoid: Text and lists stretched across the window; a width of its own (880, 920, 960, 1120)
rules.do: `content-sm`, `content-md` or `content-lg`, centered, at least `page-margin` on each side; full width only for workbench pages

rules.rule: Every general page has the same top
rules.why: When the top changes per page, the title jumps between pages.
rules.avoid: A page with its own top padding or title style; a breadcrumb bar
rules.do: The title row from the page frame, at the same place on every general page; `PageTitle` draws the title

rules.rule: One right pane, in the layout
rules.why: A second panel beside the content competes with the right pane and squeezes the content.
rules.avoid: A page that draws its own panel beside the content; a panel squeezed into a narrow window; the right pane stacked under the body
rules.do: The right pane, one thing at a time; an overlay with the scrim when there is no room; a drill-in with Back on compact

rules.rule: Fade only the edge that can scroll
rules.why: A fade says there is more this way.
rules.avoid: A fade on an edge that cannot scroll
rules.do: `useScrollFadeEdges` with `.ag-scroll-fade`

rules.rule: The agent chat sits next to its item
rules.why: The user asks about the open item, so the item stays in view and the header says what the agent sees.
rules.avoid: An agent chat in a stacked route or a dialog, or that does not name the item
rules.do: The right pane; a drill-in with Back on compact; the item named in the header; the same Composer; on compact, Back returns to the item and the draft stays

rules.rule: One item on the bottom edge
rules.why: The thumb lands on the bottom edge, so whatever sits there is the main action.
rules.avoid: Two things on the bottom edge (a composer and a floating New); a bottom nav bar
rules.do: The composer entry or one primary action; another primary action goes in the compact header or the content

rules.rule: The compact header is one 44px bar
rules.why: A compact window has little height, and the compact header is on every screen.
rules.avoid: A tall header; 44px icon buttons; two titles
rules.do: One 44px bar, the kit's compact icon buttons, one leading button, one title, at most two actions

rules.rule: Menu or Back, never both
rules.why: Two leading buttons make the user guess which way each goes.
rules.avoid: Back and the menu together; the menu on a detail page
rules.do: The menu on top-level pages; Back alone on detail pages and drill-ins

rules.rule: Menus and dialogs come from the kit
rules.why: The kit turns them into bottom sheets. A hand-made variant drifts.
rules.avoid: A popover made for an expanded window on a compact one; a hand-made compact variant
rules.do: The kit menus, selects and dialogs

rules.rule: Use the real viewport
rules.why: `100vh` hides content under browser bars and the notch.
rules.avoid: `100vh`; fixed bars without safe-area padding
rules.do: `svh` or `dvh`; `env(safe-area-inset-*)`

rules.rule: Fields show 16px text on touch
rules.why: iOS zooms the page when a field under 16px gets focus.
rules.avoid: Fields under 16px on touch; a taller field on touch
rules.do: 16px text under `pointer: coarse`, at the same height (the kit does it)

rules.rule: No action only on hover
rules.why: Touch has no hover.
rules.avoid: Actions shown only on hover
rules.do: Shown on focus too, and always under `pointer: coarse`

rules.rule: Animate a view swap, briefly
rules.why: A short fade and slide shows that something changed.
rules.avoid: An instant swap of one view for another; a duration or an easing written in a component
rules.do: A 120–200ms fade and 4px slide from `useMotionPresets()` (`src/lib/motion`); package code uses the `duration-*` and `ease-*` theme variables

rules.rule: No bounce, no attention-seeking motion
rules.why: Motion that repeats or overshoots pulls the eye from the work.
rules.avoid: Bounce, overshoot, shaking; a ping, a scaling dot, a spinning ring or gradient
rules.do: The three durations with `ease-out` or `ease-in-out`; still at rest; live activity is a spinning `circle-notch` or a 1.5s opacity pulse on a status dot; under reduced motion the new state shows without the movement

rules.rule: A caret shows where its panel is
rules.why: The caret says a panel opens there, then points back at the trigger while it is open.
rules.avoid: A caret that points the same way open and closed
rules.do: Phosphor `CaretDown` that turns 180° while open (`ag-caret`)

rules.rule: Overlays unfold from what opened them
rules.why: A panel that grows out of its trigger shows where it came from.
rules.avoid: A menu or popover that grows from its center or appears from nowhere
rules.do: `ag-overlay-motion` from the trigger's edge; only dialogs open from the center

rules.rule: The control answers in its own place
rules.why: The person is looking at what they clicked.
rules.avoid: A toast for Copy, a banner for a toggle
rules.do: The control changes: Copy becomes Check for 1.5s, the switch slides; the send arrow becomes Stop while the agent runs; a number counts to its new value (`useCountUp`)

rules.rule: No animation on things used many times an hour
rules.why: Any animation there makes the person wait, again and again.
rules.avoid: An animated open for the command palette or a shortcut
rules.do: It opens at once

rules.rule: A toggle shows its new state on the click
rules.why: Waiting for the server first makes every click feel slow.
rules.avoid: A spinner, then the switch moves
rules.do: The switch and its label change on the click; they go back only if the call fails

rules.rule: An expanding row points at what it opened
rules.why: The caret tells the person where the new content is.
rules.avoid: A caret that does not change open or closed; a filled triangle
rules.do: Phosphor `CaretRight` that turns 90° (`CollapseCaret`)

rules.rule: Sentence case everywhere
rules.why: In Title Case every word competes for attention.
rules.avoid: Title Case labels
rules.do: Sentence case

rules.rule: Toasts say what happened, in the past tense
rules.why: A toast confirms a result.
rules.avoid: "Success!" toasts
rules.do: What happened, in the past tense, with Undo when possible

rules.rule: Use the words users see
rules.why: Users manage connections and runs, not integration configs and invocations.
rules.avoid: System words (invocation, integration config)
rules.do: The user's words (run, connection); address the user as "you"

rules.rule: Five badge variants
rules.why: A badge color means a status. Other colors add a palette with no meaning.
rules.avoid: Categorical badge colors (blue, purple, gold), data colors on a badge, bordered tags
rules.do: `default`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`; text in `text-caption`

rules.rule: Tabs switch views of one thing
rules.why: A tab that starts an action surprises the user.
rules.avoid: Title Case tabs, an icon in every tab, an action as a tab
rules.do: Short nouns; the `line` variant on pages

rules.rule: Every icon-only button has a tooltip
rules.why: An icon alone is a guess.
rules.avoid: An icon-only button with no tooltip; a paragraph in a tooltip
rules.do: `SimpleTooltip` with two or three words and the shortcut

rules.rule: A tooltip does not cover the next action
rules.why: A tooltip over the next control blocks the user's next click.
rules.avoid: A tooltip that opens over the control the user goes to next
rules.do: Pick the side: `tooltipPlacement` on `Field`, `side` on `TooltipContent`

rules.rule: A toast confirms; it does not ask
rules.why: A toast closes on its own, so it cannot hold a decision or an error to fix.
rules.avoid: A question or a fixable error in a toast
rules.do: An inline `Alert`, or a dialog for a decision that blocks; a toast only confirms

rules.rule: Tables are rows, not a grid
rules.why: Grid lines and zebra fills add ink without meaning.
rules.avoid: Grid lines, zebra rows, dark header rows
rules.do: 36px rows, `border-muted` dividers, numbers right-aligned in `tabular-nums`

rules.rule: Code blocks are quiet and copyable
rules.why: Code is content, not decoration.
rules.avoid: A dark code slab on a light page; line numbers on short snippets
rules.do: A bordered box: a `muted` header with the label and one Copy button, the code in `text-code` on `background`

rules.rule: The command palette lists actions
rules.why: Each item reads as an action, and one wrong Enter must not delete anything.
rules.avoid: Bare nouns and destructive items in the palette
rules.do: Verb + object, grouped by object, the shortcut on the right

rules.rule: The Composer is one field with its actions inside
rules.why: One box reads as one control.
rules.avoid: Composer controls outside the field; a loud send pill
rules.do: Attach and Send inside the field; Send is the one filled button; Send is disabled while the field is empty

rules.rule: One Composer, two states
rules.why: A plain input dressed up as the entry opens something else and drifts from the real one.
rules.avoid: A plain input dressed up as the composer entry
rules.do: The Composer's collapsed state, which opens into the same component

rules.rule: The user's turn is a bubble; the agent's reply is not
rules.why: Long answers, code and tables read like a document at full width.
rules.avoid: Both sides in colored bubbles
rules.do: The user's turn on `bg-secondary`; the agent's reply as plain full-width text

rules.rule: Sizes come from the place
rules.why: The same Mark, icon or row at two sizes reads as two things.
rules.avoid: 18, 22 or 28px Marks; 15px icons; a size copied from the nearest screen
rules.do: The size whose `usage` in `theme.config.ts` names the place

rules.rule: The same thing is drawn the same way
rules.why: An entity, an action or a list drawn two ways looks like two things.
rules.avoid: The same entity, action or list drawn differently on two screens
rules.do: The same Mark, label, icon and row shape everywhere

rules.rule: Base components live only in the kit
rules.why: A second button or menu drifts from the kit on the next change.
rules.avoid: A hand-rolled button, input, menu or dialog; a copy of a kit component in a feature
rules.do: Import from `@agenta/ui/ui`; a new base component goes in the kit

terms.note: Only the Builder. Not models, not AI in general
Never a paper plane, which means Invite

terms.component: A Mark with the workspace letter
